questions.statement: Read the short text and answer the question. 'Fewer buses ran during the strike, and many workers cycled or walked instead.' What does the word 'instead' signal?
questions.context: An integrated skills task in a secondary school in San Salvador, SV.

options.text: That an alternative option was used
options.feedback: It introduces the other choice people made when the buses were not running.

options.text: That the situation was better than before
options.feedback: It marks a substitution of actions, not an improvement.

options.text: That the number of workers increased
options.feedback: Nothing in the text says anything about how many workers there were.

options.text: That the strike lasted a long time
options.feedback: The word marks an alternative, not the duration of the strike.

questions.explanation: The word 'instead' marks the alternative that people used when the first option was not available.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence with the correct form: 'By the time we arrived, the film ___ already ___. '
questions.context: An integrated grammar and writing task in a school in San Salvador, SV.

options.feedback: The present perfect links a past action to the present, not to a past moment.
The past perfect pairs the earlier action of starting with the later arrival.
The past continuous would describe an action in progress, not a completed earlier one.
The future simple cannot describe an action that preceded the arrival.

questions.explanation: A past time point given by 'by the time' calls for the past perfect, which is had plus the past participle.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Read the text and choose the best summary sentence: 'The class planted twenty saplings, watered them for a month and then handed the care of them to the younger students.'
questions.context: An integrated reading task in a secondary school in San Salvador, SV.

options.text: Trees are important for the environment in many places
options.feedback: This is a general claim the text never makes.

options.text: The younger students did not want to look after the saplings
options.feedback: The text says the opposite, since the care was handed to them.

options.text: The students planted trees and passed the care of them on after a month
options.feedback: This covers the action, the period and the result that the text reports.

options.text: The class planted trees but nothing came of the project
options.feedback: Nothing in the text suggests the project ended without result.

questions.explanation: A good summary names the action, its duration and its outcome in one sentence without adding what the text did not say.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the best sentence to include in a formal letter of complaint.
questions.context: A writing task in a school in San Salvador, SV.

options.text: Your school is a terrible place and everything about it is awful
options.feedback: The language is insulting rather than factual, which is unacceptable in a formal letter.

options.text: I cannot write a formal letter because I do not know what one is
options.feedback: The sentence is a comment about the writer rather than part of the letter.

options.text: Please stop making noise in the early morning near the hall
options.feedback: The command is too direct and lacks the formal opening a letter needs.

options.text: I am writing to report a problem with the noise from the hall, which begins before eight in the morning.
options.feedback: It states the problem with dates and times and keeps the tone factual.

questions.explanation: A formal complaint states the facts calmly, refers to the problem and asks for a solution without blaming anyone directly.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which word best joins these two ideas: 'The road was flooded. We took a long way home.'
questions.context: An integrated language task in a secondary school in San Salvador, SV.

options.feedback: A contrast would be wrong here, because the two sentences agree rather than oppose.
A concession would signal a surprising or opposing point that is absent.
A condition is not what relates these two statements about the journey.
The word marks the sequence of two events in the same journey.

questions.explanation: The two sentences are both about the same journey, so a linking word of time or addition fits between them.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Read the text and answer: 'The shop closes at seven, and the last bus leaves at half past eight.' When must a shopper leave to catch the last bus?
questions.context: An integrated reading and calculation task in a school in San Salvador, SV.

options.feedback: Arriving after the departure would mean missing the last bus of the evening.
That is the closing time of the shop, not the departure of the bus.
The departure time is half past eight, and the shopper must reach the stop by then.
No bus is mentioned after half past eight in the text.

questions.explanation: The last bus leaves at half past eight, so a shopper must be ready to leave before that time to catch it.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the report sentence: 'Attendance rose by fifteen per cent ___ the previous year.'
questions.context: An integrated writing task in a secondary school in San Salvador, SV.

options.feedback: The gerund cannot stand alone here, since the sentence needs a preposition after the figure.
The expression marks the comparison between this year and the previous one.
The bare verb would need a subject, and none fits after the figure in this sentence.
The noun would require a form such as 'in comparison', not the bare word given.

questions.explanation: A comparison with a previous measurement uses 'compared with' or 'in comparison to' after the figure.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Read the paragraph and identify the main problem it describes: 'Rainwater collected from the roof runs into the garden, but the pipe is too narrow, so after a storm the yard stays flooded for hours.'
questions.context: An integrated reading task in a secondary school in San Salvador, SV.

options.text: The pipe is too narrow to drain the yard quickly
options.feedback: The text identifies the size of the pipe as the cause of the standing water.

options.text: The garden receives too much rain
options.feedback: The text says the rainwater is collected, not that there is too much of it.

options.text: The roof is in poor condition
options.feedback: Nothing in the paragraph mentions the condition of the roof.

options.text: The yard is too small for the house
options.feedback: The paragraph concerns drainage, not the relative size of the yard.

questions.explanation: The problem is the narrow pipe, since the text states it as the cause of the flooding that follows a storm.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the best verb form to complete the sentence: 'If the committee ___ the plan, the project will begin in June.'
questions.context: An integrated grammar task in a school in San Salvador, SV.

options.feedback: Putting a future auxiliary in the if clause makes the construction non-standard in English.
The present simple in the condition clause points to a real future possibility.
The past simple would place the condition in a past context with a present result.
The present perfect would suggest the approval has already happened.

questions.explanation: In a first conditional the condition uses the present simple, so 'approves' is the correct form after 'if'.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Read the text and choose the sentence that best paraphrases it: 'Fewer people now drive to work than ten years ago, and the trend is expected to continue.'
questions.context: An integrated reading and writing task in a secondary school in San Salvador, SV.

options.text: Nobody drives to work and there are no cars at all
options.feedback: The paraphrase exaggerates the situation far beyond what the text says.

options.text: Ten years ago people drove more often than they will in future
options.feedback: The paraphrase drops the expectation and states the trend in the wrong direction.

options.text: Driving will disappear completely within the next ten years
options.feedback: The prediction is much stronger than the gradual trend the text describes.

options.text: Commuting by car is on the decline and is expected to keep falling
options.feedback: This preserves both the present trend and the expectation about the future.

questions.explanation: A paraphrase keeps the meaning while changing the words and often the sentence structure, without adding anything new.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Read the text and identify its purpose: 'Applications for the scholarship close on Friday at four in the afternoon. Late forms cannot be accepted.'
questions.context: An integrated skills task in a secondary school in San Salvador, SV.

options.text: To describe the whole scholarship programme
options.feedback: Only the closing time is given, not a description of the programme.

options.text: To persuade applicants to choose a different scholarship
options.feedback: No alternative is suggested anywhere in the text.

options.text: To inform applicants of a deadline they must meet
options.feedback: The notice states the closing time and the result of missing it.

options.text: To explain how applications are assessed
options.feedback: Nothing is said about the assessment of the forms.

questions.explanation: The text gives a deadline and a consequence, so it exists to make sure applicants act before the closing time.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'He asked whether the report ___ before the meeting, so nobody answered.'
questions.context: An integrated grammar task in a school in San Salvador, SV.

options.feedback: The perfect passive fits the report being complete before the meeting takes place.
The present perfect would place the completion at the present, not before the meeting.
The future simple does not fit a report that should already be complete.
The passive needs the past participle 'finished', not the base form 'finish'.

questions.explanation: In reported questions the word order of the direct question is kept but the auxiliary does not invert.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Read the text and choose the best title for it: 'A short account of how one school replaced its old heating system with solar panels, the cost, the time taken and the savings in fuel.'
questions.context: An integrated reading and writing task in a secondary school in San Salvador, SV.

options.text: The history of solar panels in the world
options.feedback: That would be a global history, far broader than this single-school text.

options.text: Fuel prices in the year of the installation
options.feedback: The text covers the savings, not the general price level of the year.

options.text: Three reasons nobody installs solar panels
options.feedback: The text describes a school that did install them and reports the benefits.

options.text: A school replaces its heating with solar power
options.feedback: The title names the actor, the action and the change, which is what the text describes.

questions.explanation: A title should summarise the content of the whole text in a few words without adding material it does not cover.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct sentence to open a paragraph in a report.
questions.context: A writing task in a secondary school in San Salvador, SV.

options.text: Nobody knows what the second stage of the project involved at all.
options.feedback: The sentence states ignorance rather than the content the reader needs.

options.text: The second stage of the project involved rebuilding two classrooms.
options.feedback: The sentence states the subject of the paragraph in clear, specific terms.

options.text: This paragraph is the second one in the document being written.
options.feedback: That describes the position of the paragraph, not its content.

options.text: As explained above in the previous document, and again below.
options.feedback: The sentence points elsewhere instead of stating what the paragraph covers.

questions.explanation: A report paragraph opens with a clear statement of what that section covers, so the reader knows what to expect.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Read the text and answer the question. 'Prices fell during the summer but rose sharply before the holidays.' When did prices rise?
questions.context: An integrated reading task in a school in San Salvador, SV.

options.feedback: The text sets the sharp rise in the period immediately before the holidays.
Prices fell during the summer, which is the opposite of a rise.

options.text: At the start of the summer
options.feedback: The beginning of the summer is not associated with any rise in the text.
The text says nothing about a rise after the holidays finished.

questions.explanation: The rise happened before the holidays, since the summer fall is contrasted with a sharp rise at that later point.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct preposition: 'The project has been delayed ___ a shortage of materials.'
questions.context: An integrated grammar task in a secondary school in San Salvador, SV.

options.feedback: 'At' cannot follow 'due to' when naming a cause, and the preposition here is fixed.
'Of' is not the preposition used in 'due to' when a cause is named.
'Due to' introduces the cause and is followed by the noun phrase naming the shortage.
'From' expresses a starting point or a source, not the cause of a delay.

questions.explanation: A cause is introduced with 'because', 'due to' or 'owing to', and 'due to' is followed directly by the noun phrase.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Read the text and identify the writer's attitude: 'The scheme has run smoothly for a year, although two minor repairs were needed in that time.'
questions.context: An integrated reading task in a secondary school in San Salvador, SV.

options.feedback: Nothing in the sentence criticises the scheme as a whole.
The praise for a smooth year is qualified by the admission of two repairs.
The sentence evaluates the scheme, so it is not neutral.
The wording is measured and factual rather than emotional.

questions.explanation: The writer is broadly positive about the scheme but acknowledges a small drawback, which is a balanced tone.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: '___ the heavy traffic, the bus arrived fifteen minutes late.'
questions.context: An integrated grammar task in a school in San Salvador, SV.

options.feedback: 'Due to' introduces the cause of the delay before the subject of the main clause.
'Due of' is not an expression; 'due to' names a cause.
'Due with' is not standard usage for a cause and would be understood as owing to a thing.
'Due in' would refer to a time limit rather than the cause of the delay.

questions.explanation: The cause here is the traffic itself rather than a person, so 'due to' is the natural connector.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Read the text and choose the most appropriate word to complete the report: 'The new system is expected to ___ operating costs by half.'
questions.context: An integrated vocabulary and writing task in a secondary school in San Salvador, SV.

options.feedback: The gerund cannot follow 'to' here, since the verb needs the base form.
'Cut' is irregular, and its past form is 'cut' rather than 'cuted'.
'Cut costs by half' is the standard collocation for reducing an amount of spending.
'Cut off' means to disconnect or interrupt, not to reduce an amount.

questions.explanation: To reduce an amount, English uses 'cut' or 'reduce', and 'cut ... by half' expresses a fall to a proportion of the original.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Read the text and choose the best response to the complaint: 'The parcel has not arrived and the deadline for the competition was Friday.'
questions.context: An integrated reading and writing task in a secondary school in San Salvador, SV.

options.text: Many parcels are delayed and this is a common problem for everyone.
options.feedback: A general remark excuses the delay without offering any solution.

options.text: You should have ordered the parcel earlier than you did.
options.feedback: The reply blames the customer instead of addressing the failure.

options.text: The competition rules are published and available on the website.
options.feedback: Pointing to the rules does not answer the complaint about the missing parcel.

options.text: We have checked with the courier and a replacement will be sent this week.
options.feedback: It gives the action taken and the next step, which resolves the complaint.

questions.explanation: The reply states what has been done so far and what will happen next, which is what a complaint response owes the writer.
questions.subject: ingles
